bug_semantics: A remote caller could supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) target in GET /api's url query parameter. PullMD passed that value to its server-side web extractor and returned the fetched content without rejecting loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata destinations or revalidating redirect targets, so a request such as /api?url=http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data could disclose cloud instance metadata and reach other internal services.
flaw_origin: The root release commit wired req.query.url directly from server.js into extractWebFn(url), while lib/web.js wrapped globalThis.fetch only with a timeout and then called fetchFn(url, { headers }). It added no URL-scheme, hostname, DNS-result, IP-range, or redirect-hop policy between attacker input and the outbound request; that unsafe fetch design, rather than a later refactor or move, is the causal origin.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d shows human author and committer syswave-dev <syswavedev@gmail.com> and the complete message "Initial public release"; there is no bot identity, Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/issues/41 gives the exact GET /api metadata-service payload and says the endpoint fetched and returned raw metadata; first-party PR https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/pull/42 identifies the unvalidated GET /api and MCP read_url paths and the required fix, and https://github.com/AeternaLabsHQ/pullmd/releases/tag/v3.3.0 names commit 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e as the v3.3.0 security release. At BIC 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, server.js:164-170 creates GET /api and reads req.query.url with only a presence check, server.js:288-290 calls extractWebFn(url), and lib/web.js:164-174 selects globalThis.fetch, adds only timeout handling, and fetches the supplied URL. git log -S'const res = await fetchFn(url, { headers });' --all --reverse -- lib/web.js returns only 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d; git log -L 505,506:lib/web.js and -L 519,519:lib/web.js from vulnerable tag commit 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5 both trace the fetch setup/call to root commit 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d. git rev-list --parents -n 1 on the BIC prints only the BIC SHA, proving it has no parent; git diff-tree --root --name-status shows both server.js and lib/web.js as A against the empty pre-root tree, directly proving the vulnerable path was absent before it. The BIC's package.json is version 1.0.0, git tag --contains the BIC includes v1.0.0 through vulnerable v3.2.0, v3.2.0 resolves to 33f19479f1bf1e0b9b6a67126f830017eb3a99c5, and v3.3.0 resolves exactly to fix 96448894cc93ccecb0bdcbf263a9d25390a8455e; git tag --contains the fix starts at v3.3.0 and excludes v3.2.0. The fix directly adds lib/ssrf.js, validates the URL before /api cache access, wraps the web fetch with redirect-hop validation, covers MCP/Reddit/Playwright paths, and bumps package.json from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0.
reasoning: The disclosed attack path is causal and direct: attacker-controlled req.query.url enters GET /api, survives only a non-empty check, reaches extractWebFn, and becomes the destination of Node's outbound fetch; the response is converted and returned. The v3.2.0 tree still blames the decisive unchecked fetch setup and call to 196cdd4e4191b073cd4f1762a35936471d1f2a5d, and both -S and -L history identify that root commit as the first writer rather than any later orchestration, auth, release, move, or refactor commit. Because the BIC is a parentless repository-creation commit, introducer_parent is necessarily null; root diff verification against the empty tree establishes parent absence, and there are no squash-member commits to decompose. The advisory's named patch is also the direct source fix and the v3.3.0 tag target, while v3.2.0 points to its immediate parent, establishing the vulnerable/patched boundary. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object: its human author/committer and trailer-free message contain no AI signal. Any disclosure associated with the later fix is outside the BIC and is not used. Therefore the smallest proven BIC is human-authored and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
